chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: Night-people talk and acting differently in dives
summary: Danny explains the joking, dozens and looseness of night people and how you must behave carefully in sleazy joints.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: But if you had been around and seen how Underworld, Nightlife people kid and joke, and they talk about... The women, they'd talk about other women. Nobody got mad. Talk about her clothes, you know, what she was doin', who's she shackin' up with. And they're playing the dozens and they talk.

You can't do that around Day People, though -- polite people. You can't come in somebody's house and... I've had cats, night people come in my house, and I have to tell them "Shh. Watch how you talk." Because there's a looseness.
Sure. You can't talk that way in the daytime.

Yeah. Well, that's the difference with Night people. If you know that, you know how to act. If you walk in a joint, and it's some sleazy joint, and you go in, you know you act cautious when you go in there. You act different than when you walk into a church.
Look at the dives we've been in in different towns. You have to know...watch where the windows are at when you go in ...(?)...
